messages.subject: Error in building unmarkedFramePCO
parts:
I have survey data of horseshoecrabs from a long term sampling initiative (~18 years). The crabs were not the primary target of the sampling, but were recorded anyway - but as a result the data is very zero-inflated. I have experimented with simple occupancy and colext models but have come to the conclusion that we're probably violating the closure assumption too much.
So I want to give the Dail & Madsen model a try (since we're mostly interested in trends over time anyway), but I am running into issues with the creating the unmarked dataframe. My data is in long format:

3       1 2014-07-01 0 0.3333333      0      0      0 0.000000000 0.0000000  160      3        1.3     6        12       30.60 8.40     36.9
4       2 2014-11-22 0 0.4491525      0      0      0 0.008474576 0.1101695  160      1        0.7    11         9       16.60 8.15     32.2

etc

"grid_id" is the site identifier, then date, "n" is the count, then site variables and then observation level variables.
(initially I had year and day of the year (Julian date) in there, as a leftover from my colext modeling, but I turned those into dates).

When I use
occu_file <- formatLong(select_data_occ_year, type="unmarkedFramePCO")
I get
Error in unmarkedFramePCO(y = c(0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L,  : 
  argument "numPrimary" is missing, with no default
When I add numPrimary though, as 
occu_file <- formatLong(select_data_occ_year, type="unmarkedFramePCO", numPrimary=18)
I get
Error in formatLong(select_data_occ_year, type = "unmarkedFramePCO", numPrimary = 18) : 
  unused argument (numPrimary = 18)

So now I am very confused! I get a similar response when using csvToUMF().
I suppose there is something wrong with the setup of my original dataframe, but I don't know what. In general I have a hard time figuring out how these functions "know" what my primary periods (years) are. Sampling is repeated throughout the year at the sites, but not all on the same day and the same amounts - but I understand that is not so much an issue (and I assume secondary sampling refers to the max number of samples in a year per site).

Any help would be so much appreciated...

Hi Geraldine,

I think this may be a simple fix. ‘formatLong’ doesn’t currently allow the user to pass extra arguments like ‘numPrimary.’ But it should, as many of the ‘unmarkedFrame*’ building functions take extra arguments, some without defaults.

I’ll take a quick stab at fixing it on Monday, and post back here if I make any progress.

Best,
Adam

messages.subject: Re: Error in building unmarkedFramePCO
parts:
Geraldine,

This turned out to be a bit more involved than I'd hoped. But I think I've made some progress.

Can you try installing this version of unmarked. You'll need the newest version of the devtools package as well to avoid some bugginess in the install.

install.packages("devtools")

devtools::install_github("adamdsmith/unmarked", ref = "reshape2")
library(unmarked)

Here's a data frame that attempts to capture the essence of yours. formatWide now seems to work fine on it... Note that `formatWide` will throw a warning about attributes not being identical across variables. This results from the fact that you have both categorical and continuous covariates, and can be ignored.

dates <- seq(as.Date("2000/1/1"), as.Date("2018/1/1"), "months")
sim_sampling <- function() sort(sample(dates, 25, replace = FALSE))

set.seed(1)
crabs <- data.frame(grid_id = rep(1:4, each = 25),
                    sDate = c(sim_sampling(), sim_sampling(), sim_sampling(), sim_sampling()),
                    n = rnbinom(100, mu = 2, size = 1),
                    site1 = rep(sample(LETTERS[1:2], 4, replace = TRUE), each = 25),
                    obs1 = round(rnorm(100), 2))

(occu_file <- formatLong(crabs, type="unmarkedFramePCO", numPrimary = 18))


I'd very much appreciate if you would test it on your full data set and confirm that the results make sense. Admittedly, I have little experience with unmarkedFramePCO structure. In particular, I can't advise on whether specifying `numPrimary` alone and letting the constructor function generate the `primaryPeriod` matrix is the right decision in your case or not.

Regards,
Adam

A question about how to set up the file though: right now I have columns with year, site id, Julian date, count, site variables and observation variables. I ordered the data by year, then site id and removed the year column. Applying formatLong() gave me 19.33 secondary survey periods though  (each row is 348 values). Some background: my sites do not all have the same number of surveys each year. The way I did it manually, was to take the site and the year with the most surveys (which was 29 surveys), and use 29 slots for each year, fill them with the counts and leave NAs if there were less than 29 surveys. This then made a vector with 18 x 29 = 522 values for each site. See attached test.csv file. The formatLong() table looks very different though (also attached formatLong_file.csv). Both files are only the y values (the counts).

This turned out to be a bit more involved than I'd hoped. But I think I've made some progress.

Can you try installing this version of unmarked. You'll need the newest version of the devtools package as well to avoid some bugginess in the install.

install.packages("devtools")

Here's a data frame that attempts to capture the essence of yours. formatWide now seems to work fine on it... dates <- seq(as.Date("2000/1/1"), as.Date("2018/1/1"), "months")
sim_sampling <- function() sort(sample(dates, 25, replace = FALSE))

set.seed(1)
crabs <- data.frame(grid_id = rep(1:4, each = 25),
                    sDate = c(sim_sampling(), sim_sampling(), sim_sampling(), sim_sampling()),
                    n = rnbinom(100, mu = 2, size = 1),
                    site1 = rep(sample(LETTERS[1:2], 4, replace = TRUE), each = 25),
                    obs1 = round(rnorm(100), 2))

(occu_file <- formatLong(crabs, type="unmarkedFramePCO", numPrimary = 18))

Regards,
Adam

Hi again Geraldine. I received your data. Thanks for sending it.

Due to the unevenness of the sampling within and among primary periods, I have little expectation that the relatively simplistic `formatLong` will construct your `unmarkedFramePCO` object correctly without passing a custom `primaryPeriod` matrix. In your case, that `primaryPeriod` matrix would a 53 x 18*29 matrix identifying the primary period of each secondary sampling event. That doesn't sound like much fun to create... 

So I think your best bet is to follow Andy's advise of creating each piece separately and passing them directly to the `unmarkedFramePCO` constructor function.

Best of luck,
Adam

Geraldine,

This turned out to be a bit more involved than I'd hoped. But I think I've made some progress.

Can you try installing this version of unmarked. You'll need the newest version of the devtools package as well to avoid some bugginess in the install.

install.packages("devtools")

devtools::install_github("adamdsmith/unmarked", ref = "reshape2")
library(unmarked)

Here's a data frame that attempts to capture the essence of yours. formatWide now seems to work fine on it... Note that `formatWide` will throw a warning about attributes not being identical across variables. This results from the fact that you have both categorical and continuous covariates, and can be ignored.

dates <- seq(as.Date("2000/1/1"), as.Date("2018/1/1"), "months")
sim_sampling <- function() sort(sample(dates, 25, replace = FALSE))

set.seed(1)
crabs <- data.frame(grid_id = rep(1:4, each = 25),
                    sDate = c(sim_sampling(), sim_sampling(), sim_sampling(), sim_sampling()),
                    n = rnbinom(100, mu = 2, size = 1),
                    site1 = rep(sample(LETTERS[1:2], 4, replace = TRUE), each = 25),
                    obs1 = round(rnorm(100), 2))

(occu_file <- formatLong(crabs, type="unmarkedFramePCO", numPrimary = 18))


I'd very much appreciate if you would test it on your full data set and confirm that the results make sense. Admittedly, I have little experience with unmarkedFramePCO structure. In particular, I can't advise on whether specifying `numPrimary` alone and letting the constructor function generate the `primaryPeriod` matrix is the right decision in your case or not.

Regards,
Adam

On Tuesday, November 6, 2018 at 2:03:40 PM UTC-5, Adam Smith wrote:
Hi again Geraldine. I received your data. Thanks for sending it.

Due to the unevenness of the sampling within and among primary periods, I have little expectation that the relatively simplistic `formatLong` will construct your `unmarkedFramePCO` object correctly without passing a custom `primaryPeriod` matrix. In your case, that `primaryPeriod` matrix would a 53 x 18*29 matrix identifying the primary period of each secondary sampling event. That doesn't sound like much fun to create... 

So I think your best bet is to follow Andy's advise of creating each piece separately and passing them directly to the `unmarkedFramePCO` constructor function.

Best of luck,
Adam
